Freytag's Pyramid

Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026)

Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton · Written by Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers · 145 minutes

  1. 1Expositionintroducing

Outer conflict

Who is the telepath taking over people's bodies, and what is the “V-Max” they are looking for?

Inner conflict

Peter Parker or Spider-Man? Does he have to silence one to be the other?

Shape of the pyramid

The climax comes at 1:57 of a 145-minute film. The climb is long and the descent is short.

1

Exposition

→ introducing

For four years nobody has remembered Peter Parker, and he has given his whole life to being Spider-Man.

  • Four years have passed since Doctor Strange's spell. To protect MJ and Ned, Peter has chosen not to reintroduce himself to them.
  • In the opening montage Peter reads the letter he wrote to MJ in voice-over. Meanwhile Spider-Man takes down the city's criminals one by one: Scorpion, Tombstone, Boomerang, Tarantula, Ramrod and the ninjas of the Hand.
  • He works alongside the police, and Detective Jean DeWolff trusts him. The city hands the key to the city to a hero whose name it does not know.
  • Peter Parker's own life is empty. He follows MJ and Ned's years at MIT on social media, visits Aunt May's grave regularly and ignores his headaches.
Why this stage?
It introduces the rule of this world (everyone has forgotten Peter) and the starting balance: Spider-Man is thriving, Peter Parker has no one.
Supporting scene
The Marvel Studios logo plays footage from the earlier films, and Peter fades out of every shot. The film shows the forgetting in its very first seconds.
2

Inciting Action

→ ignites

A tank crashes into a DODC prison, and Peter meets a telepath who jumps from body to body.

  • 0:09 A stolen tank rolls through Manhattan. While trying to stop it, Spider-Man also has to keep Frank Castle (the Punisher) from hurting bystanders.
  • The tank crashes into a prison run by the Department of Damage Control (DODC). In the driver's seat is an elderly woman who remembers nothing.
  • 0:13 Peter realises he is facing a telepath who enters people's bodies and hops from one to the next. The telepath cannot get into Peter's mind, but the attempt throws him back into his memories of May. Scorpion escapes and the mission fails.
  • At her “office” in a bathhouse, Yelena Belova tells Peter that other DODC sites have been attacked too, and that the attacker is looking for something called “V-Max”. DODC director Bill Metzger says he has never heard of it.
Why this stage?
The first event that breaks the balance. An enemy appears who cannot be beaten with fists, because the enemy is invisible and hides inside innocent people. The film's outer question starts here: who is the telepath, and what is V-Max?
Supporting scene
The same method returns through the film, each time closer to Peter: the telepath takes a stranger, then Scorpion, then MJ, and finally Banner and Frank.
3

Rising Actions

→ interests build

As the telepath closes in, Peter's body changes and the danger reaches MJ.

  • 0:26 MJ and Ned graduate from MIT and move back to New York. Peter runs into them and sees MJ kiss her new boyfriend.
  • 0:33 Peter goes home devastated and wakes up changed: his senses are painfully sharp, organic web glands have opened in his wrists, and at times his eyes turn completely black.
  • The telepath attacks another DODC site through a possessed Scorpion. Peter cannot control his new powers, beats Scorpion brutally and injures a police officer without meaning to. DeWolff tells him to get himself under control.
  • Peter visits Bruce Banner, who now teaches quantum mechanics at Empire State University. Banner shows him the inhibitor that keeps the Hulk down and asks a question: what if the thing he is trying to suppress is something that needs to be expressed? Peter builds his own inhibitor anyway.
  • While Peter is testing the device, the telepath finds his apartment and learns about MJ from the unsent letter. The telepath takes over MJ's body, pretends for a moment to remember Peter, kisses him, mocks him and nearly kills her.
  • Peter saves MJ and identifies the telepath: a young mutant named Jean Grey. He takes MJ to Frank Castle's hideout. MJ helps him finish his inhibitor and build a “universal inhibitor” that can shut down anyone's powers.
Why this stage?
Obstacles pile up and the two lines join: the telepath outside, Peter's changing body inside. Each step is more personal than the last: first the city, then Peter's own body, then MJ.
Supporting scene
At home Peter watches a nature documentary about spiders. It plants the idea that the change is part of his nature and not a malfunction, and Banner's question picks it up.
4

Complication

→ main problem

Peter captures the telepath, then learns he helped the wrong side and cannot win MJ back.

  • 1:24 Jean enters DODC headquarters in control of Bruce Banner. His inhibitor is removed, her intrusion breaks his mind, and the Savage Hulk that nobody can control comes out. The Hulk attacks Peter inside the building.
  • While Peter fights the Hulk, Jean jumps into Frank Castle and makes him open the vault where the DODC agents are hiding.
  • 1:25 Peter stops the Hulk by calling to the Banner inside him: It's me, Peter. Then he puts the universal inhibitor on Jean, and Metzger knocks her out with a tranquilliser. Before she passes out she says one name: “Sara”.
  • Metzger says Sara was an old colleague who crossed his mind while Jean was possessing him.
  • 1:29 MJ has found the letter. Peter apologises and tells her he loves her. She does not remember him and does not feel the same. Still, she invites him to the apartment she shares with Ned, and a masked Peter grows close to both of them.
  • When MJ mentions that she remembers nothing from the time she was possessed, Peter understands that Metzger lied. Redacted DODC files found by Yelena show the truth: Sara is Jean's older sister, also a telepath, and the DODC kidnapped her.
Why this stage?
The main problem comes fully into view. Peter seems to have won, but everything is knotted the wrong way: the person he caught is a lonely teenager looking for her sister, the agency he helped is the real offender, MJ does not love him, and he has silenced his own power with a device.
Supporting scene
Frank Castle's hideout, a houseboat called “Golden Girl”. Frank trusts no one and lives alone, and he shows where the same road could take Peter.
5

Climax

→ turning point

Jean realises her sister is dead, freezes everyone around her and asks Peter the film's question.

  • 1:37 Flashback: the two sisters discovered their powers together, their mother abandoned them, and the DODC experimented on them to copy their abilities. Sara died in the test chair.
  • Now Jean sits in the same chair: Metzger experiments on her at the Roosevelt Island facility. She notices the worn label on the air vent in her cell: “Ventmax”. “V-Max” was the last thing Sara saw before she died, sent to Jean mind to mind.
  • In her rage Jean creates a psionic field that spills beyond the facility. Everyone inside it freezes except Peter, including MJ and Ned.
  • Peter apologises. Jean refuses and sends the Hand ninjas at him. Their weapons shred his synthetic webs. Wounded, Peter takes off his mask.
  • 1:57 Jean asks: Are you Peter Parker, or Spider-Man? Peter tears off his inhibitor: I'm both.
Why this stage?
The turning point. The film's inner question is asked out loud for the first time, and Peter makes a choice he cannot take back: he stops suppressing his power and accepts both sides of himself. Everything that follows is a result of this answer.
Supporting scene
The scene in Banner's office. There Peter decided the answer was suppression and put the inhibitor on. The climax reverses that scene: he removes the device with his own hands.
6

Reversal

→ sudden change

Peter stops fighting and invites Jean into his mind, and the hostility dissolves at once.

  • The situation flips: organic webs are not affected by the web-shredding weapons. Peter disables the Hand without killing a single ninja.
  • He stops Jean from killing Metzger.
  • 1:59 He chooses to let her into his mind and stops fighting her. Jean finds herself inside one of Peter's memories, where May says: We love you, not because you're special, but because you're you.
  • Peter and Jean understand each other through what they have lost. He tells her You have me, and she gives up on killing Metzger.
Why this stage?
The sudden change produced by the decision at the climax. Peter, who was being hunted, takes control; the conflict turns from fighting to understanding; and the enemy becomes someone Peter protects.
Supporting scene
At their first contact the telepath tried to force a way into Peter's mind and failed, and later forced a way into MJ's. Here Peter opens the door himself.
7

Falling Actions

→ conflict unravels

Frank's bullet hits Peter, the psionic field collapses, and the city keeps watch over its hero.

  • 2:05 Frank Castle has been watching from a distance through his rifle scope. He does not trust the truce and fires at Jean.
  • Peter senses the bullet, shields Jean and is badly wounded. The psionic field collapses at that moment and everyone who was frozen is released.
  • A horrified Frank rushes Peter to hospital.
  • While doctors fight to keep Spider-Man alive, New York fills the streets: candlelight vigils are held and the Empire State Building is lit red and blue. From far away, Jean uses her powers to keep Peter alive.
Why this stage?
The conflict starts to come apart, at a price. Jean is no longer a threat and the psionic field is gone. One question is left: will Peter live?
Supporting scene
The tank scene. There Peter stopped Frank from harming bystanders. The same contrast pays off here: Frank wants to solve it by killing, Peter by protecting, and Peter takes the bullet.
8

Resolution

→ release

Peter wakes up, sees how much the city loves him and promises to stop carrying everything alone.

  • Peter wakes up in hospital. A remorseful Frank is at his bedside and tells him Jean kept him alive from a distance. A friendship begins between them.
  • To protect Peter's identity, Frank puts on the mask and stands at the window. Peter slips into the crowd and, for the first time, sees from the outside how much the city loves him.
  • Jean leaves the city. Metzger disappears and the DODC is placed under investigation.
  • At May's grave Peter promises to stop trying to do everything alone. While he recovers, he agrees to leave a robbery to DeWolff.
Why this stage?
The tension is released. Both the outer conflict (Jean and the DODC) and the inner one (loneliness and the belief that “I have to do everything myself”) are closed.
Supporting scene
The opening montage. There Peter went to the grave alone, looking for comfort, and ran to every crime by himself. The same cemetery and the same DeWolff now show the opposite.
9

Denouement

→ “happily ever after?”

The old handshake with Ned comes back; MJ and the future stay open.

  • Peter runs into Ned at a bodega and introduces himself as a stranger. Without thinking, the greeting turns into their old secret handshake. Ned's face lights up: Peter!
  • MJ sits on the roof of Midtown High, holding a necklace she cannot remember receiving.
  • The film does not say that the memories are fully back. It shows that the spell has cracked and leaves the rest open.
  • In the post-credits scene, Ned's Spidey Tracker app marks Spider-Man's location as “off-planet”.
Why this stage?
The new balance. The question mark in the class notes makes sense here. Peter is no longer alone, but MJ still does not remember him and a new journey is about to begin.
Supporting scene
Ned's Spidey Tracker app. Ned built it to find and thank the hero who saved him and his class in high school. The person he was looking for was Peter all along.
